SearchHow we decideRulings

Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Body, health & movement

swell verb

also swell up, puff up, swelling up

classical

Plaut. Pers. 2.5.11: quid hoc hīc in collō tibi tumet?
Verg. A. 2.273: pedēs (Lewis & Short)

tumeō, tumēre

verb, second conjugation

swell, be swollen

(vōx plērumque poētica et post Augustum in ōrātiōne solūtā (Lewis & Short); apud Plautum dē corpore)

Of a part of the body, a sponge, a bud, the sea. The perfect tumuī is that of tumēscō.

Other words

  • tumēscō, tumēscere, tumuī — begin to swell, swell up

    verb, third conjugation · also used · classical · Verg. G. 2.479; Tac. H. 2.77: vulnera (Lewis & Short)

    (vōx plērumque poētica et post Augustum in ōrātiōne solūtā (Lewis & Short))

  • intumēscō, intumēscere, intumuī — swell up

    verb, third conjugation · also used · classical · Ov. F. 1.215: venter; Plin. NH 20.51 (Lewis & Short)

    (vōx plērumque poētica et post Augustum in ōrātiōne solūtā (Lewis & Short))

Examples

  • Quid hoc hīc in collō tibi tumet?

    What’s this swelling here on your neck?Plaut. Pers. 2.5.11

  • haec tibi sorte datur tergendīs spongia mēnsīs ūtilis, expressō cum levis imbre tumet

    this sponge falls to your lot, useful for wiping tables when, squeezed of its water, it swells up lightMart. 14.144.1–2

See also swollen, bump.
